text:
maria: Heads-up — getting Xid spikes after rolling driver 535.54 to eu-west-1 GPU fleet at ~07:45 UTC. Triggered the gpu-xid-alert (pager).

maria: Alerts hit ~40 hosts, mostly A100s on k8s nodepools gpu-eu-prod.

sam: Copy. Which Xid codes are trending? 31 again?

maria: Mostly Xid 31 and a handful of 43. Example from dmesg on host gpu-eu-12:

```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3d:00): 31
[ 1234.567901] NVRM: GPU 0000:3d:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.567905] nvidia 0000:3d:00: GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.568000] nv_peer_mem: allocating memory failed
```

maria: Also seeing repeated `nvidia-mig-manager` restarts on the same nodes.

devon: What changed in the rollout? Driver 535.54 + kernel 6.2.11? Or only driver?

maria: We rolled driver 535.54 (package id rdx-driver-535.54-2026.03.11) across eu-west canary -> prod. Kernel stayed at 5.19 for most nodes, but a small batch on nodepool gpu-eu-hot was on 6.2.11.

sam: Could be driver + kernel combo causing kernel oops leading to Xid. Any kernel oops in dmesg?

maria: Yes, there's a stack trace snippet: `gpudrv+0x1a2b3` followed by `nv_kern` frames and `oops: Unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference` in one node.

andrea: Runbook check: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/gpu-xid-incident — do we need to cordon/godown nodes?

maria: I'm cordoning high-Xid hosts now and evicting pods with `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`.

leo: Prom query I used to quantify scope:

```
sum by(instance, xid) (increase(nvidia_device_xid_total[10m]))
```

leo: Trend: spike from ~2/min to ~120/min in eu-west over 20m.

sam: Good. Can we reduce blast radius by throttling the rollout? Pause?

maria: Paused the rollout at 07:52 UTC. Canary (10 nodes) shows same pattern on 3/10 -> probable regression.

devon: Try temporary NCCL env knobs on canary pods: `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` and `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` to see if inter-GPU comms are implicated.

andrea: Also try forcing `CUDA_DISABLE_MPS=1` on a single node to rule out MPS interactions.

maria: Did both on two canary nodes — no immediate drop in Xid rates.

sam: Ok next step: rollback driver on canary hosts to previous version 535.27 and observe. Who can run that?

leo: I can do rollback on 3 canary nodes. Using the edge: `apt-get install rdx-driver-535.27 --allow-downgrades` then `systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced`.

infra-bot: Scheduled job rollback-driver-eu-canary started by leo at 08:10 UTC. Job ID: J-98532.

maria: After rollback on 3 nodes Xid counts dropped to baseline within 5m. Confirmed.

sam: That strongly implicates 535.54. Open a vendor ticket with Nvidia and attach logs.

maria: Case opened with Nvidia. Case ID NV-2026-00421. Attached dmesg, `nvidia-smi -q` dumps, and kernel oops snippets.

nvidia-rep: Thanks — we are triaging. Can you provide `modinfo nvidia` output and `rm /proc/driver/nvidia/version`? Also need `/var/log/kern.log` slice around the Xid.

maria: Uploaded requested artifacts to the case. Link: https://support.nvidia.com/case/NV-2026-00421

leo: As a defensive measure I lowered the Prom alert thresholds to avoid noisy paging but keep slack channel alerts: changed gpu-xid-alert from 5->30/min per region for now.

andrea: Please note — update the runbook: add step to pause driver rollout and rollback canary if Xid rate > 20/min and reproduce on >=20% canary.

sam: I've updated the monitor doc and created a short playbook snippet in the runbook (lines added).

maria: Post-rollback summary: rolled back 24 hosts in eu-west (all prod canary and hot nodes), Xid graphs flattened over 30m. We are keeping 10 hosts at 535.54 for vendor debugging.

devon: Cost/ops note: rollback meant re-running kernel module builds and node reboots — about ~2 hours of drain/reboot per node overhead. Flagging in infra operations budget.

maria: Next steps: 1) Keep prod fleet at 535.27 until Nvidia confirms fix. 2) Add an automated canary sanity check to rollout pipeline that watches `increase(nvidia_device_xid_total[10m])`. 3) Postmortem doc.

leo: I'll add the canary check into our rollout pipeline (patch MR #8421).

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1307 (GPU driver regression — eu-west). Pager cleared at 10:12 UTC after rollback.

andrea: Assigning postmortem to devon + maria. Please include diff of node kernel/driver combos and the exact hosts that stayed at 535.54 for vendor.

maria: Noted. Will compile logs and timelines. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

leo: Leaving one monitoring tweak: add `avg over 5m` smoothing to detection query so a transient spike doesn't page.

sam: Good catch. Also add a label in alerts for `driver_version` so we can filter by rollout.

maria: Uploading final timeline and logs to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-1307/postmortem

devon: Closing loop — keep me in thread when Nvidia responds.

nvidia-rep: Received new logs. Nvidia engineering assigned. Will update within 24-48h.

maria: Thread closed for immediate ops. Will reopen if vendor finds root cause or if we see reoccurence.
